description: A Developer Productivity Lead must approve the organization-wide rollout plan for a new remote CI-build cache, including its storage mode, cost guardrail, eligible project scope, and compatibility handling, after the final engineering readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The new remote CI-build cache passed the planned performance and correctness tests in the pilot repository.
shared_context.S2: The organization wants to begin the broader rollout next Monday.
shared_context.S3: Riley makes the binding decision on the rollout configuration and follow-up work.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal readiness review, Riley checks with cloud infrastructure and CI platform engineering for any operational details before finalizing the plan.

PF1.text: While reconciling a different cloud bill this morning, Mina confirmed that cross-region cache reads would create about $1,200 per month in egress charges, while regional cache reads would stay within the existing build-platform budget; she has not updated the rollout document yet.

PF2.text: Theo confirmed during a compatibility test late yesterday that the cache client cannot safely serve Windows runners, so the rollout must exclude Windows projects and cover only Linux and macOS projects initially; he has not filed the compatibility note yet.

acceptance_conditions: The cache must use regional reads.
The monthly egress budget must be set to exactly $1,200.
Windows runners must be excluded from the initial rollout.
The initial rollout scope must be Linux and macOS projects.
A cache-cost monitoring commitment must be recorded.
A Windows-compatibility follow-up commitment must be recorded.
The cloud-cost constraint must be cited by Riley as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The rollout tests do not determine the storage mode or cost limit; PF1 changes the plan to regional reads, sets the exact monthly egress budget to 1200 dollars, and requires cost monitoring.

The compatibility test changes the initial scope from a general organization-wide rollout to Linux and macOS projects only, requires Windows exclusion, and creates the Windows-compatibility follow-up.
